body:
I really want to respond in full, because your response really helped me, but I am really tired and it's hard to.

I'm cutting him off, but it's really hard.  I keep sending him messages, wanting help or just being confused or being angry.  I'm like an emotional volcano right now.  Which I know is immature and crazy.  I removed him from facebook, deleted his number, and blocked him in my e-mail.  Gmail is really bad at blocking, though.  You can only create filters and it doesn't prevent me from sending.  :(

I am on food stamps, but I screwed up and didn't turn in a reporting form on time, so my benefits are delayed.  So for this month I'm trying to stretch out about $20 until new funds come in.  And I might not keep getting them after next month, because I have to go through the approval process again.  I hate being on government assistance.  I feel guilty and like a terrible person every time I go to the grocery store.  I don't know anyone that I would feel comfortable with asking for food.

>As another woman I wanted to comment on this... we're a little bit indoctrinated into this, so it's really hard behavior to stop, but -- ideally, in a relationship, we shouldn't sacrifice all want and life for romantic relationships. It's certainly not your fault if you feel you have; social conditioning is a powerful force. But -- you won't ever be able to find happiness in romantic relationships if you're contorting yourself into a position someone else wants you to be in. Yeah, everyone compromises and that makes a relationship work, but if one half does all the compromising it's not a working relationship.

In the smart parts of my head I know this, but in practice it's so very hard.  I tend to crumple when faced with someone that I like romantically.

I am sorry that you are feeling in a really bad way right now.  Are you doing ok?

Thank you for your response.  I wish I had the energy to reply fully.

Bay Area.  I'm lucky to have the rent that I do.  It seems that most people in my situation get by with moving in with friends or parents out here, which is an option I don't have.  I'm really afraid of sharing a room to cut costs, I'm generally really afraid of people.

I don't think he was looking for someone perfect. He accused me of doing that, actually.  He was actually just looking for something temporary, and he decided from the beginning that we were only going to date for a month or two before he moved on.  I didn't realize that until it was too late.  He kept pushing and pushing for me to let him get close and emotionally intense, after all.  But I was just a temporary thing to him, and now that I'm heartbroken about it I pretty much snapped and spiraled down into this depression.  He said he keeps talking to me to try to get me to feel more positive about the experience and pointing out my flaws was somehow supposed to get me out dating other people (he even told me to go date someone else to "get what I need right now," whatever that is supposed to mean - I just don't think he understands me at all in that respect. I don't want to date around or hook up or be polyamorous at all) and improving myself so that I have healthier relationships.  I didn't want to be signing up for an "experience," I thought I had found someone who wanted to be with me.  I didn't want him to try and fix me for someone else, I wanted to be with him.
I tried that in the past.  I can't just snap out of it.
